note: Example: A^N with inner product sum of (x n)* (y n) is a Hilbert A-module. The type is Mathlib `WithCStarModule A (Fin N -> A)`, notation C-star-mod(A, Fin N -> A), the same type synonym 32I is rendered on and the one 36III `selfDual_pi` (TowardsVN.lean:527) and 33I use as their witness; completeness, the Hilbert as opposed to pre-Hilbert half, is the CompleteSpace instance the synonym carries at a complete A. DIFFERS ON THE DISPLAYED FORMULA, and only there. Mathlib builds the inner product on a Pi type coordinatewise (Analysis/CStarAlgebra/Module/Constructions.lean:235, inner x y = sum over i of inner (x i) (y i)) out of the inner product of A over itself, which is `inner x y := y * star x` (ibid.:79, `WithCStarModule.inner_def` at ibid.:91). So our A^N carries inner x y = sum over n of (y n) * star (x n) where 32II displays sum over n of star (x n) * (y n) -- the two factors in the other order. Both satisfy every clause of 32I -- for Mathlib's, inner x (a * y) = (a y) star x = a * inner x y, so it too is additive and A-linear in the second argument with the scalar on the left, and it is positive on the diagonal and star-symmetric, and the two are each other read in the opposite algebra, so they agree exactly when A is commutative and not otherwise. The same mismatch is already recorded one row down at 32IV, where it is harmless because C[0,1] is commutative; here A is arbitrary, so it is not. Nothing downstream is wrong -- `selfDual_pi` proves r x = inner A y x with y i = star (r (e i)), which unfolds to r x = sum over i of (x i) * r (e i), the correct identity for OUR inner product -- but a reader who takes 32II literally and expects star (x n) * (y n) will read every A^N computation in this file and in TowardsVN.lean backwards.
